essential: The voyage along Multiplicity has touched race and sex. Pumpelly says Willard Gibbs got help from Pearson's Grammar of Science. Adams reads it in Paris until December 26.

His mathematical ignorance denies him the right to judge. The Grammar seems an enlargement of Stallo but marks a historic English stride after twenty years of silence. Langley's Smithsonian papers (Crookes, Roentgen, Curie) prepared him.

Pearson's attack on Kelvin's textbooks and the deep-sea-fish circle of the senses. Include the Pearson quotes, attributed: order belongs to the mind, there is no inference beyond the senses, chaos. Keep Adams's crystal objection.

English thought forbids knowing the unknowable yet thinks about it. Everyone from Pythagoras to Hegel sailed into the supersensual calling it unity. Only the Church and Pearson agree. The Tennyson lines, briefly.
The change of 1900 was long prepared (1893, radium in 1898). The uniformitarians' contradictions were wrecked by rays. Science is adrift on a sensual raft, as in 310, and Adams is on the raft.
Germany: Haeckel's whispered avowal that substance is enigmatic. Mach rejects matter (Matter is Motion). They agree with Pearson that the supersensual is unknowable.
France: Poincare. Nature no longer loves simplicity; some approach to unity has been made; but the endless alternation of simple and complex turns the historian green.
Complexity has always been true. Poincare on mathematical continuity as symbols and on Euclid as convenient. The genealogy of Truth from Aquinas to Pearson.

The historian is a mere instrument of measure (keep a shortened version of the catalogue of ignorance). Motion and matter: 'we are probably incapable of discovering'. Radium as the next point since Zeno.
The historian must not seek truth. Thought moves like a cannon-ball: 310, 1500, Galileo and Bacon, then 1900 snaps. Balfour's dating.

The child of 1900 is born into a multiple world where order is artificial compulsion. It explains man's fiendishness, but the despotism of order lies ahead (the physicists' phrase). He wishes to escape.

The pearl-oyster image and woman's ordered universe. Lucretius' Venus, quoted in reduced form. 'Her supersensual chaos killed her.' Adams as a ball of vibrating motions at the feet of the Virgin or of Poincare. The mind cannot be satisfied: merge or succumb.

voice_profile: Third-person self-portrait in which 'Adams', 'the student', 'the historian', 'the insect' or 'the gray-headed moth' is mocked by his own narrator. The prose is ironic and aphoristic. Each paragraph builds a long periodic sentence through dashes and semicolons toward a deflating epigram. Adams compulsively converts persons and politics into physics: force, inertia, attraction, mass, acceleration and the 'larger synthesis'. He constantly professes ignorance, and that ignorance is itself the method. Paradox is treated as orthodoxy. Learned allusions (Seneca, Pascal, Aquinas, Lucretius, Faust) are deployed with self-deprecating humour. Quotations from real sources are marked and attributed. Double hyphens and French or Latin tags are part of the texture.
